look_here_first: Inspect opposite, thick, glossy leaves 3–6 inches long: look for a distinct opaque 1–2 mm rim at the blade edge and 6–8 pairs of lateral veins. Confirm large terminal flower/fruit panicles and woody tree-like habit.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Native to eastern Asia; introduced in North America. Learner-approved encounter/comparison taxon, not a confirmed target-zone native.

morphology_keys.habit: Broadleaf evergreen shrub or small tree; can reach a large tree-like crown.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, simple, entire, thick and glossy, usually 3–6 inches long; conspicuous opaque margin rim, 6–8 pairs of lateral veins; veins sunken beneath.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small white four-lobed flowers borne in large terminal panicles, roughly 5–8 inches long.
morphology_keys.fruit: Numerous blue-black drupes in persistent terminal panicles.
morphology_keys.stems: Tan twigs with lenticels; leaves largely glabrous.

comparisons.key_distinctions: L. sinense typically has thinner 1–3 inch leaves with hairs along the underside midvein and hairy petioles, shorter 2–3 inch panicles, and a shrubbier thicket habit. L. japonicum can have thick leaves but lacks the same prominent opaque marginal rim; check venation and flowers.
comparisons.cautions: Privets vary with pruning, shade, and juvenile growth. Use multiple mature leaves, nodes, venation and panicle structure; do not use fruit color alone.

diagnostic_image_needs: Matched mature leaf top and underside with scale
Leaf margin, midvein hair and petiole macro
